purpose: attribute WITHIN-analyzer cost for the php lane; NOT the end-to-end throughput record
sample: 200 tracked .php files, deterministic strided slice of 3231
interpretation: msPerFile is NOT comparable to the differential baseline's 6.3-9.5 ms/file. Two measured reasons: (1) this includes parse, which the baseline's warm-pool loop excludes; (2) the strided slice is file-EQUAL not byte-equal, so it is dragged by the large vendored sources under tools/.phpstan/ and tests/**/vendor/ that a first-N sorted slice would miss. Use bytesPerFile and the PHASE SPLIT, not msPerFile, to compare. The phase split is the robust result: it is a ratio over one measured run and is insensitive to which files were sampled.
note: parse is tree-sitter WASM and sits OUTSIDE the analyzer. postPasses walk the SYMBOL TABLE, not the tree, so they cannot be the cost driver the way a repeated full-tree walk can — every namedChild()/childForFieldName() crosses the JS<->WASM boundary, which is why a separate full-tree walk (collectPhpFileScope) is reported separately from the fused mainWalk rather than merged into it.
